fair_value_reason: NTM EPS at Sep 2027 ~$14.25 (0.25 x FY27 $13.2 + 0.75 x FY28 ~$14.6) x 26.25x = $374. Cross-check: consensus-based NTM EBITDA ~$6.85B x 16.6x = $113.7B EV, less ~$18.4B net debt (consensus, interpolated to Sep 2027), over ~251M shares = $380. Weighted 60/40, ~$376, rounded to $375 (~5.4% above spot, plus a ~0.8% dividend). Versus the agents' $366-381 (mean $373.2), this trims agent_1's EBITDA to consensus and sets the multiple at a ~5% de-rating, between agent_3's 25.5x and agent_2's 26.5x.
supervisor_summary: Round 2 converged on my round-1 view (fair values $366-381, mean $373; P(>= spot) ~0.545), but part of that is anchoring on my own judgments, so I treat it as 2-3 independent views, not 5. Fact-checks: consensus Sep-2027 NTM EBITDA is ~$6.82B, so agent_1's $7.05B is ~$13/share too high. Kalshi's liquid 2027 recession contract is ~20% (verified), the WSJ survey gave 25% in July, and RSM's 30% is stale, which supports the agents' ~15-22% bear weights. A ~5% de-rating to ~26.25x is the defensible middle of their 25.5-26.5x range. Fair value is ~$375 (~5% upside plus a 0.8% dividend), the thesis break is $270, and I keep the mean ladders with low confidence.
key_drivers: Earnings: FY26 guide $11.64-11.81 adj. EPS / $5.97-6.03B EBITDA. Consensus EBITDA is $6.46B (FY27) and $6.93B (FY28), so Sep-2027 NTM is ~$6.82-6.85B and NTM EPS ~$14.25, driven by ~4.5% net rooms growth, card fees and ~4%/yr share shrink.
Multiple: spot is ~27.7x NTM EPS / ~17.3x NTM EBITDA. A ~5% partial reversion to ~26.25x / 16.6x gives ~$375. Holding the multiple gives ~$395; 22x gives ~$315.
Macro: Kalshi prices ~20% for a 2027 technical recession (liquid). The WSJ July survey gave 25%, the NY Fed curve model 14%. This supports a ~20% bear weight, not the earlier 35%.

2027 U.S. demand: CoStar +2.1% U.S. RevPAR, tough World Cup comps, and Marriott's 'flattish' 2027 group pace (which turned up in July) lagging Hyatt/Park. Hilton's Oct 27 and Marriott's ~early-Nov Q3 calls are the next checks.
Easy H1 2027 Middle East comps (Q2 -43%, July -12%) versus the Bonvoy owner dispute as a tail risk to the card-fee line.
